title: Sixteen Mornings and One Grey Hill
subtitle: 清晨与时序 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 清晨与时序（生活与学习·时间与作息）
meta: 主题语境：清晨与时序（生活与学习·时间与作息）　|　核心词汇：dawn　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dawn 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the shepherd ① watched a dawn that no farmer in the valley would have waited for, and he said the watching was the whole of the watch. The ② dawn, meaning the light and not the beginning, ran sixteen mornings and stayed undescribed; dawn, he said, is the only thing in a valley that is judged by how long it is left unreported.

Every ③ dawn in that valley had the same grey hill above it, and the ④ dawn at the end, meaning the one before the shearing and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever remembered twice. A dawn, his daughter said, is nine parts cold and one part somebody willing to watch; the shepherd said the watching is the part that fills sixteen mornings.

My grandfather meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dawn was the whole of the year, meaning the beginning and not the light. The ⑥ dawn, meaning the beginning and not any of that, is the only thing in a year that everybody greets and nobody keeps; dawn, he said, is either something you watch or the only word that means both a light and a beginning. He said the beginning is the part they remember.

By 1957 the ⑦ dawn had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the grey hill. The ⑧ dawn of the whole thing, the shepherd wrote in June, was one valley and sixteen mornings of watching; dawn, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to watch. She said the watching was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dawn I remember is the one at the end, which broke in 1968 and is still described as the coldest in the valley. A ⑩ dawn, his daughter said in 1970, is the only thing that improves by being watched; every dawn, she said, is a beginning that has agreed to look like a light. She said the beginning was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 黎明；拂晓（指山谷里出现的那一次）
B. n. 曙光（指那道天光本身，与那个开端相对）
C. 固定搭配：watch a dawn 守候一次黎明
D. n. 黎明（指剪羊毛前那一个早晨）
E. n. 黎明；天光（抽象总称，指一条山谷的全部晨色）
F. n. 黎明（指日记里写到、被记下的那一次）
G. n. 开端；起始（指一年之初的那个起点）
H. n. 开端（抽象总称，指人人迎接却无人留住的那个开始）

items.q: watched a dawn that no farmer in the valley would have waited for
The dawn, meaning the light and not the beginning
the dawn was the whole of the year
the dawn had become a line in a diary
The dawn of the whole thing
A dawn, his daughter said in 1970

answers.why: watch a dawn 意为“守候一次黎明”，1950 年牧羊人守候了一次山谷里没有一位农夫肯等的黎明。
dawn 意为“曙光”，指那道天光本身而不是那个开端，它历经十六个早晨而从未被描写。
dawn 意为“黎明”，指那条山谷里每一次黎明，每一次上方都是同一座灰色的山。
dawn 意为“黎明”，指剪羊毛前那一个早晨，是唯一有人记起过两次的。
dawn 意为“开端、起始”，指一年之初的那个起点，祖父说这个开端就是那一年的全部。
dawn 意为“开端”，指人人迎接却无人留住的那个开始而不是那道天光，是一年里人人都迎接、却无人留住的东西。
dawn 意为“黎明”，指日记里写到、被记下的那一次，到 1957 年这次黎明成了日记里的一行。
dawn 意为“黎明、天光”，牧羊人六月写道，整件事的晨色是一条山谷和十六个早晨的守候。
dawn 意为“黎明”，我记得的是末尾那一次，1968 年破晓，至今仍被说成山谷里最冷的一次。
dawn 为抽象总称，他的女儿 1970 年说，一次黎明是唯一会因为被守候而变得更好的东西。
